results.title: LeanPRM
results.content:
3SortSome failures are just bad Lean, not bad math. A second model reads the compiler output, repairs pure syntax once, and keeps only failures where the mathematics is at fault.

The LeanPRM pipeline: a paired proof attempt, Lean checking, a review of the first failure, and a verifier trained on the natural-language steps.

The pipeline on one proof. Lean finds the first failing step, the reviewer confirms it is a mathematical error, and the verifier trains on the prose with those labels.

## A labeled proof

The proof from the figure above, as the verifier sees it. Click a step to see the Lean behind it and what the checker decided.

Theorem (NuminaMath). In a finite group where every automorphism is a power map x ↦ xm, any two elements commute. [...] | ModelQwen3-4B, 500 updates | LeanPRM-Benchexact | Hard2Verifybalanced acc. | ProcessBenchavg. F1 | PRMBenchfirst error | IMO-GradingBenchbalanced acc. |

5. 5We now claim that x^m = x by asserting that conjugating x by y returns x itself, that is y·x·y⁻¹ = x, and therefore the power x^m must coincide with x.✗

   Lean tactic

   ```
   have keyx : x ^ m = x := by have hxx := hm x rw [MulAut.conj_apply] at hxx rw [← hxx]; group
   ```

   Lean and reviewer

   Nothing earlier shows that conjugating x by y gives back x. That is the claim being proved, so this step assumes its own conclusion. Lean rejects it, and the reviewer confirms the problem is the mathematics, not the encoding.
6. 6Therefore x·y = x^m·y by the claim x^m = x, and x^m·y = y·x because y·x = x^m·y; chaining these equalities shows x·y = y·x, so x and y commute.✗

results.title: Leanmeds is rated "Poor" with 2.6 / 5 on Trustpilot
results.content: Evaluating 161 reviews, most reviewers were unhappy with their experience overall. Consumers frequently stated that payments were processed immediately upon signing up, yet trying to reach customer support or getting timely responses proved extremely difficult and frustrating. People also encountered major delays when scheduling initial appointments and experienced severe issues regarding prescrip tion orders or missing medications altogether. Some reviewers were happy with the professional medical providers who listened closely to their concerns and answered all questions thoroughly. Others also appreciated the quick email communication, helpful guidance, and efficient telehealth visits that ultimately made the overall process much easier to successfully navigate for patients.See more

results.title: Paper page - LeanPRM: Lean-Grounded Process Supervision for Natural Language Proof Verification
results.content: AI systems now write long and difficult mathematical proofs, and checking their step-by-step validity is becoming a bottleneck. A learned verifier could check proofs cheaply, but training one requires a correctness label on every step, and such labels are hard to obtain for open-ended proofs. Existing methods take them from human annotators, which is costly, or derive them from final answers, which proofs do not have, and formalizing each proof in Lean requires expert effort. We introduce LeanPRM, a framework that uses the Lean proof assistant to create step-level labels for natural-language proofs. A model writes a natural-language proof together with a paired formal proof, without feedback from Lean. Lean then labels every step, and a second model discards failures caused only by the [...] and a second model discards failures caused only by the formal syntax, so that the negative labels mark errors in the mathematics. LeanPRM contains 10,634 proofs with 152K labeled steps and no human annotation. A Qwen3-4B verifier trained on LeanPRM raises exact step-label accuracy on a held-out set of 200 proofs (LeanPRM-Bench) from 48.2 to 74.7, as opposed to 60.3 when the same base model is trained on PRM800K. It also selects better proofs in best-of-N selection on IMO-level problems, and outperforms the PRM800K-trained verifier on three of four external verification benchmarks. Training on LeanPRM improves verifiers at every size from 0.6B to 8B parameters on LeanPRM-Bench, Hard2Verify and IMO-GradingBench. Given the labels need no human annotation, LeanPRM can grow with the supply of [...] no human annotation, LeanPRM can grow with the supply of formal statements, offering a path to step-level feedback on AI-generated proofs that are hard for humans to check.
